claim: Boot address echo is updated when the write handshake completes (HOST_GO fall) instead of with the write, so while HOST_STATUS acks the k-th byte uo_out still shows k-1.
spec_ref: docs/architecture.md:Pipeline/LOAD (boot) -- "chip: (internally) sync HOST_GO, write byte, increment counter, update the uo_out echo, THEN assert HOST_STATUS / host: wait for HOST_STATUS=1 ... -> read uo_out, now guaranteed valid -> lower HOST_GO"

why_survives.directed: test_boot_echo_and_saturation reads uo_out only after load_byte returns, i.e. after the ack has cleared, by which time the late echo has landed; every other directed test ignores the echo and uo_out is re-cleared at START.
why_survives.random: fast_boot pokes SRAM directly and never runs the per-byte LOAD handshake (out of the golden model's scope).
why_survives.board: Chip.boot uses the same load_byte helper and never reads the echo.
why_survives.formal: No props file constrains uo_out during LOAD; reset props check uo_out only at reset and after leaving LOAD.
